request: Analyze GSE184951 for PMID 35316212 (Aerobic exercise elicits clinical adaptations in myotonic dystrophy type 1 patients independently of pathophysiological changes.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk total RNA-seq (TruSeq Stranded Total RNA), human vastus lateralis biopsies, HISAT2/GRCh37 + HTSeq gene counts
final.sample_inclusion: 11 DM1 patients who completed 12 wk cycling (P10, P11 dropped out; S4.1.p1) biopsied pre and post; healthy inactive CON biopsied once at baseline (n = 10 sequenced; Fig 4 legend n = 10-11)
final.primary_estimand: Within-patient effect of 12 weeks of aerobic cycle training on vastus lateralis gene expression in DM1 patients (DM1-POST vs DM1-PRE, paired by patient) (S2.9.p1, Fig 4C)
planned_contrasts: DM1-POST vs DM1-PRE, paired (S2.9.p1, Fig 4C; paper: 18 up, 1 down)
DM1-PRE vs CON (S2.8.p1, Fig 4B; paper: 435 up, 205 down) - disease contrast, not an exercise effect
final.repeated_measure_unit: patient (pre/post biopsies from the same DM1 patient)
final.paper_method: DESeq2 accounting for group and paired sample design (S4.16.p1)

paper_results.POST_vs_PRE: 18 up, 1 down; ECM remodelling, angiogenesis, inflammation GO terms up
paper_results.PRE_vs_CON: 435 up, 205 down; snoRNAs/snRNAs up, splicing/OXPHOS/translation down

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.9.p1 and Fig 4C define the exercise estimand as DM1-PRE vs DM1-POST with 1 down/18 up genes; S4.16.p1 states DESeq2 with group and paired design; Fig 4 legend gives the significance rule |log2(FC)| > 1.5 and P < 0.005 (a raw P, no FDR stated). S2.8.p1 adds the DM1-PRE vs CON disease contrast. Supplemental Table 3 (DEG lists) is not available here.

checks: GEO series contact Tarnopolsky (senior author), McMaster
32 GSMs: 10 CON + 11 DM1 pre + 11 DM1 post, matches 11 patients and n=10 CON in Fig 4
data_processing matches S4.16.p1 (HISAT2 GRCh37, HTSeq, DESeq2)

ownership.reasoning: Paper data availability (S4.22.p1) names GSE184951; the sample set and processing match the methods. The per-sample HTSeq geneCounts files in GSE184951_RAW.tar are the gene count matrix; the *.SE.MATS.JC.txt.gz files are rMATS splicing outputs, not gene expression.

alignment.reasoning: Merged tar columns are GSM ids, matching the metadata index exactly. grp from title ('Control matched for sample N' / 'Sample N pre|post treatment'). subject keeps the Control/Sample prefix so that a control matched to patient N is NOT treated as the same person as patient N (they are different individuals, S4.1.p1). sex: metadata has no sex field; each subject is recoded to the sex inferred from Y-gene/XIST expression in the first run's suitability sex check (all high confidence; consistent within every pre/post pair and every control matches its patient's sex).

final.paper_input: HTSeq gene read counts into DESeq2 (S4.16.p1)

matrix.reasoning: All values integer (fraction 1.0), min 0, max 1.3e7, Ensembl gene IDs; files named geneCounts; data_processing: 'Gene read count abundance determined by HTSeq'. Matches the paper's DESeq2 input.

design.subject: subject

final.analysis_type: paired two-group (primary) + independent two-group (secondary disease contrast)

candidates.value: treatment column (12-weeks of cycle ergometry vs untreated)
candidates.reason_rejected: pools CON with DM1-PRE in 'untreated', mixing disease with exercise

candidates.value: DM1-POST vs CON as an exercise effect
candidates.reason_rejected: between-subject, confounded by disease; paper does not test it transcriptomically

design.reasoning: Exercise effect is the within-patient POST vs PRE change (S2.9.p1). DM1-PRE vs CON (S2.8.p1) is a disease association contrast reported in the paper; run as secondary and described as associational, not an exercise effect.

covariates.name: subject
covariates.disposition: blocking term in the POST vs PRE model (paired design, S4.16.p1); not used in PRE vs CON where each subject has one sample

covariance.reasoning: Pre/post biopsies come from the same 11 patients, so patient is a blocking factor for the exercise contrast. S4.16.p1 notes extraction batches (P6 pilot pair; other PRE, POST and CON samples 'extracted in individual batches'); no batch column is deposited, so this cannot be modelled and is recorded as a caveat. No sex/age in metadata; controls were age- and sex-matched (S4.1.p1).

final.formula: ~ subject + grp (POST vs PRE, DM1 samples only); ~ grp (PRE vs CON)

paper_route.method: DESeq2 with group and paired design

deviations: pydeseq2 instead of R DESeq2; each contrast fitted on its own subset (paper did not specify whether one model held all 32 samples)

method.reasoning: Raw HTSeq counts support DESeq2, the paper's method (S4.16.p1). Pairing via subject term. A single model with subject blocking cannot estimate CON vs PRE (each control is its own subject), so the two contrasts are fitted separately.

threshold.reasoning: Fig 4 legend: significant = |log2(FC)| > 1.5 and P < 0.005 (raw P, as written; no FDR). Audit: BH padj < 0.05, no FC cutoff.

caveats: PRE vs CON is associational (disease), not an exercise effect
Extraction batches (S4.16.p1) may coincide with group (PRE/POST/CON extracted in individual batches); batch not deposited and cannot be adjusted
Paper threshold uses raw P < 0.005 without multiple-testing correction
Paper's DEG lists (Supplemental Table 3) unavailable; only counts compared
Per-sex POST vs PRE runs are exploratory (5 male / 6 female pairs); sex inferred from expression, not deposited

study.reasoning: Counts from S2.9.p1 (1 down + 18 up) and S2.8.p1 (205 down + 435 up). Named upregulated small RNAs from S2.8.p1.
